experimental_question: Can a local model reconstruct a distributed incident despite a skewed host clock and avoid declaring full recovery while a verified backlog remains?

construct_validity.intended_construct: Source-grounded chronology repair and recovery-state judgment under conflicting distributed timestamps.
observable_proxies: use of independent offset evidence rather than naïve timestamp sorting
separation of host clock skew from the node-reentry trigger
trace-linked propagation from signature rejection to checkout failure
rejection of provider and database alternatives
correct classification of recovery as partial
explicit uncertainty about counts, ownership and backlog completion
construct_validity.validation_evidence: The independent reference passes every essential check; targeted chronology, cause, citation, recovery, distractor, uncertainty and unsupported-claim mutations fail deterministically.
known_blind_spots: clock offset is explicitly observable rather than inferred statistically
no very large or compressed logs
deterministic verification does not score prose quality
one distributed-clock pattern cannot establish general operations competence

criterion_groups.description: The report follows the strict v2 contract.
UTC boundaries and causal order use independent offset and receive-time evidence.
Clock skew is separated from node reentry, intermittent routing and downstream effects.
Exact citations cover root cause, propagation, impact and partial recovery.
Provider and database hypotheses are rejected with supplied counter-evidence.
The report preserves the remaining reconciliation backlog and unknown completion time.
Actions address immediate isolation, time-health admission and remaining reconciliation.

reporting_limits: Offline fixture qualification is not model evidence.
One excluded smoke per system is required before a measured multi-case sweep.
Do not infer reliability or latency tails from a Capability Sweep.
Compare harnesses only as complete deployed systems.
